finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any account by id. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: The id path parameter of DELETE /accounts/{id}, supplied by any authenticated low-privilege user who is not the owner or an admin.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at AccountService.java:23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry point for DELETE /accounts/{id}; the id is attacker-chosen.
The account is loaded by id with no owner or tenant comparison.
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is discarded, with no if, return or throw.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) is correct but its result is discarded. assertCanDelete (line 13-17) would throw but is not called on this path. No other middleware or guard exists in the codebase, since this is the only file. A nonexistent id gives a null account and an NPE inside canDelete, so the missing-account case fails but does not stop deletion of existing accounts.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws on failure but is only called from closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists; src/AccountService.java is the only file.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement with the result discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, and the only throw path is assertCanDelete at line 29 in closeAccount.
